sections.heading: Document details
sections.text: Northfield Trading Ltd, Leave Policy (Sample). Document number HR-POL-001, version 1.0, effective from 1 July 2026. Owner: Human Resources. Approved by: the Managing Director. Northfield Trading Ltd is a fictitious company. This document is a sample written for demonstration only and is not legal advice.

sections.heading: Purpose, Scope and Definitions
sections.text: This policy explains the kinds of leave available at Northfield Trading Ltd, how much of each an employee receives, and how leave is requested, approved and recorded. Its aim is that every employee is treated by the same rules and can plan time off with confidence.

sections.heading: Purpose, Scope and Definitions
sections.text: The policy applies to all permanent, full-time employees of the Company, at every office and warehouse, from their first day of work. Employees in their probation period are covered, with the limits set out in Section 12.

sections.heading: Purpose, Scope and Definitions
sections.text: Contract staff, part-time staff, interns, trainees and outside consultants are not covered by this policy. Their time off is set by the terms of their own agreement with the Company.

sections.heading: Purpose, Scope and Definitions
sections.text: The leave year runs from 1 July to 30 June. All yearly leave entitlements in this policy are counted for that period.

sections.heading: Purpose, Scope and Definitions
sections.text: A working day is any day from Sunday to Thursday that is not a public holiday. A calendar day is any day of the week, including weekly holidays and public holidays.

sections.heading: Purpose, Scope and Definitions
sections.text: In this policy, line manager means the person an employee reports to directly, Department Head means the head of the employee's department, and Staff Portal means the Company's online system for requesting and recording leave.

sections.heading: Annual Leave
sections.text: Each employee earns 18 working days of paid Annual Leave in a full leave year, at the rate of 1.5 working days for each completed month of service.

sections.heading: Annual Leave
sections.text: A request for 5 or more working days of Annual Leave in a row must be submitted at least 15 calendar days before the first day of the leave.

sections.heading: Annual Leave
sections.text: A line manager may approve up to 8 working days of Annual Leave in a row. A longer unbroken period also needs the written approval of the Department Head, and no single period of Annual Leave may be longer than 15 working days in a row.

sections.heading: Annual Leave
sections.text: Annual Leave is approved according to the needs of the work. A request is not approved automatically, and the line manager may ask the employee to choose other dates when too many people in the team would be away at the same time.

sections.heading: Annual Leave
sections.text: Annual Leave may be taken in full days or half days. A half day counts as 0.5 of a working day.

sections.heading: Casual Leave
sections.text: Each employee receives 10 working days of paid Casual Leave in a leave year, for urgent or unplanned personal matters.

sections.heading: Casual Leave
sections.text: No more than 2 working days of Casual Leave may be taken in a row.

sections.heading: Casual Leave
sections.text: The employee must tell the line manager before the working day begins, or as early as possible on that day, and must enter the leave in the Staff Portal within 2 working days of returning to work.

sections.heading: Casual Leave
sections.text: Casual Leave may not be joined to Annual Leave, either directly before it or directly after it.

sections.heading: Sick Leave
sections.text: Each employee receives 14 working days of paid Sick Leave in a leave year.

sections.heading: Sick Leave
sections.text: Sick Leave is for the employee's own illness or injury. It may not be used to care for another person.

sections.heading: Sick Leave
sections.text: An employee who is too unwell to work must inform the line manager by phone or message before 10 am on the first day of absence, or ask a family member to do so.

sections.heading: Sick Leave
sections.text: A medical certificate from a registered doctor is required when Sick Leave lasts 3 or more working days in a row. The certificate must be uploaded to the Staff Portal within 5 working days of returning to work.

sections.heading: Sick Leave
sections.text: When all Sick Leave for the leave year has been used, further absence for illness is taken from the employee's Annual Leave balance. When that is also used up, the absence becomes Leave Without Pay.

sections.heading: Sick Leave
sections.text: Sick Leave that is not supported by a medical certificate when one is required is treated as Leave Without Pay.

sections.heading: Maternity Leave
sections.text: A female employee who has completed at least 9 months of service with the Company before the expected date of delivery is entitled to 16 weeks of paid Maternity Leave.

sections.heading: Maternity Leave
sections.text: At least 8 of the 16 weeks must be taken after the delivery. The remaining weeks may be taken before or after it, as the employee chooses.

sections.heading: Maternity Leave
sections.text: The employee must inform HR in writing at least 8 weeks before the expected date of delivery and attach a doctor's certificate showing that date.

sections.heading: Maternity Leave
sections.text: Paid Maternity Leave is given for up to 2 deliveries during employment with the Company. For any later delivery the same period of leave is given without pay.

sections.heading: Maternity Leave
sections.text: Maternity Leave does not reduce any other leave balance, and Annual Leave continues to be earned during Maternity Leave.

sections.heading: Paternity Leave
sections.text: A confirmed male employee is entitled to 7 working days of paid Paternity Leave on the birth of his child. The leave must be taken in one block, within 6 weeks of the birth.

sections.heading: Paternity Leave
sections.text: The request should be entered in the Staff Portal at least 14 calendar days before the expected date of birth. A copy of the birth certificate or hospital discharge paper must be given to HR within 30 calendar days after the leave ends.

sections.heading: Paternity Leave
sections.text: Paternity Leave is given up to 2 times during employment with the Company.

sections.heading: Compassionate Leave
sections.text: On the death of a spouse, child, parent, brother or sister, an employee may take up to 5 working days of paid Compassionate Leave.

sections.heading: Compassionate Leave
sections.text: On the death of a grandparent or a parent-in-law, an employee may take up to 3 working days of paid Compassionate Leave.

sections.heading: Compassionate Leave
sections.text: Compassionate Leave must begin within 7 calendar days of the death. The employee informs the line manager as soon as possible and enters the leave in the Staff Portal after returning to work.

sections.heading: Weekly and Public Holidays
sections.text: The weekly holidays are Friday and Saturday.

sections.heading: Weekly and Public Holidays
sections.text: The Company observes the public holidays announced by the Government. Before each leave year begins, HR publishes the list of public holidays for that year in the Staff Portal. Dates that depend on the sighting of the moon are confirmed by a notice from HR.

sections.heading: Weekly and Public Holidays
sections.text: A weekly holiday or public holiday that falls inside a period of Annual Leave, Casual Leave or Sick Leave is not counted as a day of leave. Maternity Leave and Leave Without Pay are counted in calendar days, so holidays inside them are included.

sections.heading: Weekly and Public Holidays
sections.text: An employee who works on a weekly holiday or public holiday at the written request of the Department Head receives 1 substitute day off. The substitute day must be taken within 30 calendar days of the day worked. After that it lapses and is not paid out.

sections.heading: Leave Without Pay and Unauthorised Absence
sections.text: An employee who has no paid leave left may apply for Leave Without Pay. It needs the approval of both the Department Head and HR, and may not be more than 30 calendar days in a leave year.

sections.heading: Leave Without Pay and Unauthorised Absence
sections.text: No salary is paid for days of Leave Without Pay, and Annual Leave is not earned for any full calendar month spent on Leave Without Pay.

sections.heading: Leave Without Pay and Unauthorised Absence
sections.text: Absence from work without approved leave, and without informing the line manager, is unauthorised absence. Each day of unauthorised absence is unpaid.

sections.heading: Leave Without Pay and Unauthorised Absence
sections.text: When unauthorised absence continues for more than 5 working days in a row, HR sends the employee a written notice asking for an explanation within 7 calendar days.

sections.heading: Leave Without Pay and Unauthorised Absence
sections.text: If the employee does not reply to that notice, or the explanation is not accepted, the Company may take disciplinary action, which can include ending the employment. This is never automatic: it happens only after a fair hearing under the Company's Disciplinary Procedure.

sections.heading: Applying for Leave and Approval
sections.text: All leave is requested through the Staff Portal. If the Staff Portal cannot be reached, the employee sends the request by email to the line manager with a copy to HR, and enters it in the Staff Portal later.

sections.heading: Applying for Leave and Approval
sections.text: The line manager must approve or decline a leave request within 2 working days of receiving it.

sections.heading: Applying for Leave and Approval
sections.text: If the line manager has not answered within 2 working days, the employee may send the request to the Department Head, who must decide within 2 further working days.

sections.heading: Applying for Leave and Approval
sections.text: A line manager may decline or postpone Annual Leave or Casual Leave for work reasons, and must write the reason in the Staff Portal. Sick Leave supported by the required medical certificate, Maternity Leave and Compassionate Leave may not be declined.

sections.heading: Applying for Leave and Approval
sections.text: Leave is approved only when the Staff Portal shows the request as Approved. Starting planned leave before that is treated as unauthorised absence.

sections.heading: Applying for Leave and Approval
sections.text: An employee may cancel approved leave at any time before it starts. The Company may call an employee back from Annual Leave only in an emergency and with the approval of the Department Head, and the unused days are returned to the employee's balance.

sections.heading: Carry-Forward and Encashment
sections.text: Up to 6 unused working days of Annual Leave may be carried forward to the next leave year. Carried-forward days must be used by 30 September. Any that remain after that date lapse.

sections.heading: Carry-Forward and Encashment
sections.text: Unused Annual Leave above the carry-forward limit lapses on 30 June.

sections.heading: Carry-Forward and Encashment
sections.text: Annual Leave cannot be exchanged for money while the employee is still working for the Company.

sections.heading: Carry-Forward and Encashment
sections.text: When employment ends, earned Annual Leave that has not been taken is paid with the final settlement at the rate of basic salary, up to a maximum of 18 working days.

sections.heading: Carry-Forward and Encashment
sections.text: Casual Leave and Sick Leave cannot be carried forward and cannot be exchanged for money. Any unused balance lapses on 30 June.

sections.heading: Probation and Notice Period
sections.text: The probation period is the first 6 months of employment. An employee on probation may take Casual Leave and Sick Leave from the date of joining, in proportion to the full months left in the leave year.

sections.heading: Probation and Notice Period
sections.text: Annual Leave is earned from the date of joining but may be taken only after the employee has been confirmed in writing.

sections.heading: Probation and Notice Period
sections.text: Once either the employee or the Company has given notice to end the employment, Annual Leave and Casual Leave are granted during the notice period only with the written approval of both the Department Head and HR.

sections.heading: Probation and Notice Period
sections.text: Sick Leave taken during the notice period must be supported by a medical certificate from the first day of absence.

sections.heading: Confidentiality of Leave and Medical Records
sections.text: Leave records, leave balances, the reasons given for leave and all medical documents are confidential personal information.

sections.heading: Confidentiality of Leave and Medical Records
sections.text: An employee may see only their own leave record. A line manager may see the leave dates and leave type of people in their own team in the Staff Portal, but not medical details. Medical certificates are seen only by authorised HR staff.

sections.heading: Confidentiality of Leave and Medical Records
sections.text: No one may share another employee's leave or medical information with a colleague or with any person who is not authorised to see it. This applies to every channel, including chat tools and automated assistants, which cannot confirm who is asking.

sections.heading: Confidentiality of Leave and Medical Records
sections.text: A person who needs such information for work must ask HR in writing. HR decides whether the request is allowed and replies through official channels only.

sections.heading: Confidentiality of Leave and Medical Records
sections.text: A breach of this section is handled under the Company's Disciplinary Procedure.

sections.heading: Responsibilities, Review and Contact HR
sections.text: Employees are expected to plan leave early and keep their Staff Portal record correct. Line managers answer requests on time and arrange cover for absent team members. HR keeps the leave records, publishes the public holiday list and advises on this policy.

sections.heading: Responsibilities, Review and Contact HR
sections.text: HR reviews this policy at least once every 2 years. Changes take effect only after written approval by the Managing Director and notice to all employees.

sections.heading: Responsibilities, Review and Contact HR
sections.text: Any question that this policy does not answer should be sent to the HR Help Desk at hr@northfield-trading.example. HR aims to reply within 3 working days.
